title: David with the Head of Goliath
source: Galleria Borghese, Rome (public domain). Full resolution from Wikimedia Commons: David_with_the_Head_of_Goliath-Caravaggio_(1610).jpg
caption: The severed head is the painter's own face. Caravaggio painted it while on the run, with a death sentence hanging over him. #art #arthistory #painting #history #oilpainting
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-10 (Galleria Borghese page galleriaborghese.beniculturali.it/en/?p=10534 + Wikipedia): dated 1609-10 by the museum (some scholars say as early as 1605); head of Goliath = Caravaggio's self-portrait (museum: 'the artist's last, tragic self-portrait'); 28 May 1606 killed Ranuccio Tomassoni in a brawl, sentenced in absentia to beheading; sword letters read as 'HumilitAS Occidit Superbiam' (museum: 'difficult to read', Augustine maxim); in Scipione Borghese's collection, possibly sent as a request for pardon.
Death: museum says he died 18 July 1610 in southern Tuscany, circumstances unclear; 'pardon on its way' is the usual telling, keep it loose.

slides.headline: The severed head in this painting is the painter himself
slides.sub: Caravaggio, David with the Head of Goliath, c. 1609-1610

slides.headline: Look at Goliath
slides.text: The face of the giant is widely believed to be a self-portrait. Caravaggio painted himself as the defeated, the guilty one.

slides.headline: Still alive?
slides.text: One eye is half open, the mouth hangs as if in a last breath. It is not a trophy, it is a man at the moment of dying.

slides.headline: A painter on the run
slides.text: In 1606 Caravaggio killed a man in a fight in Rome. He was sentenced to death and spent his last years fleeing from city to city.

slides.headline: David doesn't celebrate
slides.text: Look at his face: no triumph, no pride. He looks at the head with something like pity, or sadness.

slides.headline: Words on the sword
slides.text: The blade carries the letters H-AS OS, often read as a Latin phrase meaning "humility kills pride".

slides.headline: A plea for mercy
slides.text: The painting went to Cardinal Scipione Borghese, nephew of the Pope, the man who could help him get a pardon. Many read it as Caravaggio offering his own head.

slides.headline: Darkness everywhere
slides.text: No background, no landscape. Only two figures coming out of the dark, lit like a stage. Caravaggio's trademark.

slides.headline: He never got home
slides.text: In 1610 the pardon was finally on its way. Caravaggio died on his journey back to Rome, at 38.
